from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = ["A Bernoulli trial has only two possible outcomes.", 
                         "Outcomes must be either success or failure.", 
                         "Each trial maintains a constant success probability."]
        self.setup_layout("Prerequisite: The Bernoulli Trial", lecture_lines)
        
        # Elements
        coin = Circle(radius=1.0, color=BLUE)
        success_label = Text("Success", font_size=24, color=GREEN).move_to(coin.get_top() + DOWN*0.5)
        failure_label = Text("Failure", font_size=24, color=RED).move_to(coin.get_bottom() + UP*0.5)
        coin_group = VGroup(coin, success_label, failure_label)
        self.place_at_grid(coin_group, 'C3', scale_factor=1.0)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(Create(coin_group))
        self.lecture[0].set_color(YELLOW)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(Indicate(success_label, color=YELLOW))
        self.lecture[1].set_color(YELLOW)
        self.wait(0.5)
        self.play(Indicate(failure_label, color=GREY))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color(YELLOW)
        self.play(coin.animate.set_stroke(width=6), run_time=1)
        self.wait(1)

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Calculate P of X equaling k successes.",
            "Combinations count total ways to arrange successes.",
            "Multiply by probability of successes and failures.",
            "Formula combines these two distinct components.",

        ]
        self.setup_layout("The Binomial Formula Breakdown", lecture_lines)
        
        formula = MathTex(

        )
        self.place_at_grid(formula, 'C3', scale_factor=1.2)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(Write(formula), Indicate(self.lecture[0], color=YELLOW))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = ["PMF shape changes with n and p.", "Observe how bar heights shift with probability.", "The sum of all probabilities always equals one."]
        self.setup_layout("Visualizing the Probability Mass Function", lecture_lines)
        
        # Define chart
        from scipy.stats import binom
        def get_bars(n, p):
            x_vals = np.arange(n + 1)
            probs = binom.pmf(x_vals, n, p)
            bars = VGroup(*[Rectangle(height=p*3, width=0.4, color=BLUE, fill_opacity=0.7) for p in probs])
            bars.arrange(RIGHT, aligned_edge=DOWN, buff=0.1)
            return bars

        chart = get_bars(10, 0.5)
        self.place_in_area(chart, 'B1', 'E6', scale_factor=0.8)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        self.play(Create(chart))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(WHITE), self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        chart_p_low = get_bars(10, 0.2)
        self.place_in_area(chart_p_low, 'B1', 'E6', scale_factor=0.8)
        self.play(Transform(chart, chart_p_low))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(WHITE), self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        # Total probability indicator
        total_text = Text("Sum = 1.0", font_size=24, color=GREEN)
        self.place_at_grid(total_text, 'F3')
        self.play(FadeIn(total_text))
        self.wait(1)
        self.play(FadeOut(chart), FadeOut(total_text), self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(WHITE))

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Application & Wrap-up", [
            "Binomial distributions model real-world fixed trials.",
            "Useful for quality control and genetic predictions.",
            "Essential for predicting experiment outcomes accurately."
        ])
        
        # Define visual elements
        die = SVGMobject("die_face_6.svg") if os.path.exists("die_face_6.svg") else Square(side_length=0.5, color=WHITE)
        qc_icon = VGroup(Square(side_length=0.5, color=BLUE), Text("QC", font_size=12)).arrange(DOWN)
        dna_icon = VGroup(Line(ORIGIN, UP*0.5, color=GREEN), Line(UP*0.5, UP, color=GREEN)).rotate(PI/4)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(YELLOW)
        self.place_at_grid(die, 'C2')
        self.play(FadeIn(die))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(BLUE)
        self.place_at_grid(qc_icon, 'C4')
        self.place_at_grid(dna_icon, 'D4')
        self.play(FadeIn(qc_icon), FadeIn(dna_icon))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color(GREEN)
        final_text = Text("Predict Outcome = Success!", font_size=24, color=WHITE)
        self.place_in_area(final_text, 'E2', 'F5', scale_factor=0.8)
        self.play(Write(final_text))
        self.wait(2)

sections.title: Prerequisite: The Bernoulli Trial
sections.content: Define the building block: a Bernoulli trial. Emphasize three requirements: only two outcomes (Success/Failure), constant probability (p), and independent trials. Visual: A light switch flipping between On (Success) and Off (Failure).
sections.example: Flipping a fair coin: Head (Success, p=0.5) or Tail (Failure, q=0.5).

sections.title: Defining the Binomial Setup
sections.content: Introduce the Binomial Distribution as a sequence of 'n' independent Bernoulli trials. Define the random variable X as the total number of successes. Visual: A sequence of n slots filling with either 'S' or 'F'.
sections.example: A robot dog tries to jump through 5 hoops. Each attempt has a 70% success rate. X is the total number of hoops successfully cleared.

sections.title: The Binomial Formula Breakdown
sections.content: Deconstruct the formula P(X=k) = C(n,k) * p^k * (1-p)^(n-k). Explain the 'n choose k' (combinations) as the number of ways to arrange successes, and the probability product as the likelihood of that specific sequence. Visual: Animated tree diagram collapsing into the formula components.
sections.example: Calculating the probability that the robot dog clears exactly 3 out of 5 hoops: C(5,3) * (0.7)^3 * (0.3)^2.

sections.title: Visualizing the Probability Mass Function
sections.content: Explain how the distribution changes based on 'n' and 'p'. Show a bar chart transforming as 'p' shifts from 0.1 to 0.5 to 0.9. Emphasize that the sum of all probabilities equals 1. Visual: A dynamic histogram shifting shape.
sections.example: Comparing the robot dog's success probability (p=0.7) vs. a 'lucky' cat's jump probability (p=0.2) over 10 trials.

sections.title: Application & Wrap-up
sections.content: Summarize real-world use cases (Quality control, genetics, risk assessment). Recap that the Binomial distribution is essential for predicting outcomes in fixed-trial experiments. Visual: Icon cluster showing a factory line, DNA strands, and dice.
sections.example: A quality control device checking 100 microchips; using binomial distribution to find the probability of having 0 defective chips.
